web.title: List of men's footballers with 50 or more international goals
web.description:
[![Cristiano Ronaldo](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Euro_2016_Cristiano_Ronaldo.jpg/250px-Euro_2016_Cristiano_Ronaldo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Euro_2016_Cristiano_Ronaldo.jpg) [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo) holds the all-time men's international scoring record with [146 goals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_goals_scored_by_Cristiano_Ronaldo). Since October 2021, the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee) (IOC) has also been publishing a list, but only of the top 10.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men%27s_footballers_with_50_or_more_international_goals#cite_note-International_Olympic_Committee_%E2%80%93_Most_goals_in_international_football-1) [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo) of [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team) holds the all-time record with [146 international goals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_goals_scored_by_Cristiano_Ronaldo). [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team), [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_national_football_team), [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_national_football_team) and [Kuwait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait_national_football_team) hold the record of having the most players to have scored 50 or more international goals with four each. [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_national_football_team), [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_national_football_team), [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_national_football_team), [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia_national_football_team), [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea_national_football_team) and [Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thailand_national_football_team) each have three players who have achieved the feat. [Bader Al-Mutawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bader_Al-Mutawa) of Kuwait has played the most matches so far to score 50 international goals. ## History [[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men%27s_footballers_with_50_or_more_international_goals#cite_note-Imre_Schlosser_%E2%80%93_RSSSF_%E2%80%93_UEFA-11)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men%27s_footballers_with_50_or_more_international_goals#cite_note-Imre-9) He remained the highest international goalscorer for 26 years, until his fellow countryman [Ferenc Puskás](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferenc_Pusk%C3%A1s) broke the record in 1953. [[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men%27s_footballers_with_50_or_more_international_goals#cite_note-17) However, [Vivian Woodward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Woodward) scored 75 goals in 53 matches considered official internationals by the opposing sides, which would make him the first footballer to score 50 or more international goals, ahead of Imre Schlosser, and was the fastest to achieve the feat, scoring his 50th goal in his 32nd official international match, with a four-goal haul against Hungary on 31 May 1909. Puskás overall scored 84 goals in his international career,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men%27s_footballers_with_50_or_more_international_goals#cite_note-Puskas-12) and remained the highest international goalscorer for 24 years following his 84th goal in 1956 against [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_national_football_team), until [Mokhtar Dahari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mokhtar_Dahari) of [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia_national_football_team) broke the record in the [Merdeka Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merdeka_Tournament) after scoring his 85th goal on 27 October 1980 against [Kuwait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait_national_football_team); he went on to score 89 goals for his country in 142 international appearances. Daei also became the first player to score over 100 goals in international football, ending his career with [108 in total](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_goals_scored_by_Ali_Daei). He attained this in a friendly match against the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union_national_football_team) on 21 November 1965, and went on to score 77 international goals in 92 matches.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men%27s_footballers_with_50_or_more_international_goals#cite_note-Pele-38) [Malawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malawi_national_football_team)'s [Kinnah Phiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinnah_Phiri) was the first player from [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederation_of_African_Football) to score 50 international goals. Whilst it was originally believed that Phiri was also the youngest player to do so (having scored his 50th goal in a friendly match against [Sierra Leone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Leone_national_football_team) on 6 July 1978, aged 23 years, 8 months and 6 days),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men%27s_footballers_with_50_or_more_international_goals#cite_note-Phiri-39) FIFA acknowledged in 2021 that the record actually belonged to Mokhtar Dahari, who was 22 years, 8 months and 30 days when he scored his 50th goal for Malaysia against [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_football_team) on 12 August 1976.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men%27s_footballers_with_50_or_more_international_goals#cite_note-40) [Stern John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stern_John) of [Trinidad and Tobago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinidad_and_Tobago_national_football_team) was the first player from [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONCACAF) to score 50 international goals. ## By player | Rank | Player | Nation | Confederation | [Goals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scoring_in_association_football) | [Caps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cap_(sport)) | Goals
